## Rules (non-negotiable)
No code comments anywhere (Rust `//` `///` `//!`, Python `#`, TOML/YAML/shell `#`, docstrings beyond a forced one-liner); the only forced exception is one `/// # Errors` line clippy demands on a `pub fn` returning `Result`, and on a NEW fork file the ASF header plus one `///` where the fork's `deny(missing_docs)` forces it on a new `pub` item. Never delete a pre-existing comment. Reasons in the touched `map.md`s (`pins: <unit>/C-NNN`) and the ledger. Self-check before every commit: `git diff --cached | grep -nE '^\+.*(//|#)' -- '*.rs' '*.py' '*.toml' | grep -v '#\[' | grep -v noqa` prints nothing beyond the forced lines. Identity `git -c user.name="TRO-Wolf" -c user.email=64240326+TRO-Wolf@users.noreply.github.com`; the LAST line of every commit message (RePark and fork alike) is exactly `Authored-By: Muse Spark (muse-spark-1.3) <noreply@meta.ai>`; no other trailer. Never push, never `gh`, never `aws`, never `--no-verify`, never touch `.github/`; `Cargo.lock` may change ONLY through `make bump-fork-pin` after the fork side lands (see below). Maps in lockstep; no amends. `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8 RUST_TEST_THREADS=8`; three cargo builders is the box's cap and others are live — one cargo invocation at a time, in one lane at a time. Numbers ONLY from a release module (`.venv/bin/maturin develop --release`, prove `__debug_assertions__ False` and the path under your lane); load under ~16 cores during timed runs, record the 1-minute load at start and end. One Spark JVM at a time (`pgrep -af 'pyspark-shell|SparkSubmit'`, wait with a 60 s poll); ivy redirect `cp -a ~/.ivy2.5.2 <lane>/.ivy2` + `PYSPARK_SUBMIT_ARGS="--conf spark.jars.ivy=<lane>/.ivy2 pyspark-shell"`. AWS out of scope.

## The two halves (fork side first, RePark side second — two lanes)
**Fork half (F-27), lane `$HOME/repark-lanes/lanes/icescan-fork` = already cloned at the fork's current main (F-26, F-CATIO, F-28 merged; dead push URL; branch `f-27-count-star-projection` checked out).** (a) Empty projection → zero-column batches: `reader.rs::get_arrow_projection_mask` turns `field_ids.is_empty()` into `ProjectionMask::all()`; make an empty projection produce batches with the row count and no columns (arrow `RecordBatch::try_new_with_options` with `row_count`), keeping delete-vector and positional-delete application correct (they must still filter rows — measure on a DV table). (b) `IcebergTableScan::statistics()` returns exact row counts when the snapshot has no delete files, no residual filter and no limit, so DataFusion folds `count(*)` without a scan. Both with the fork's own tests (`cargo test -p iceberg` for the reader, `-p iceberg-datafusion` for the scan), ASF header on any new file, the fork's clippy/fmt gates (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`), commit on the fork lane with the same identity and no trailers. Hand the fork commit SHA back; the orchestrator pushes the fork branch, opens the fork PR and, after it merges, bumps the pin — you do NOT push.
**RePark half, lane `$HOME/repark-lanes/lanes/oc-icescan`.** (c) Consume the fork change through a TEMPORARY `[patch]`/path override to `$HOME/repark-lanes/lanes/icescan-fork` for measurement ONLY (never committed; `git diff` of `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` must be empty at hand-back) and pin the behaviour: `count(*)` on a plain Iceberg table folds (≤ 5 ms at 1e6, measured), `count(*)` on a table with a DV / positional deletes does NOT fold and answers the deleted-row-aware count Spark-equal; `count(*)` with a WHERE residual does not fold; `count(*)` after `LIMIT` behaves. (d) Small tables scan in parallel: `plan_partition_work` bin-packs to `read.split.target-size` (128 MiB) so a 1e6-row table under that size runs as ONE partition; derive a session-level split size so `|groups| ≥ target_partitions` when the table allows it (files can be split by row-group range), excluding MERGE / identity-DELETE target scans (whose partition identity the DML paths depend on — find and cite those paths). Pins: row-set identity on the partitioned bed table `t_part`, `_pos` / lineage reads over ranged splits Spark-equal, the V3 `_row_id` order pins unchanged. Fixtures from the analysis: `iceberg_read/{1e6,1e7}/t_plain/{count_star,count_id,sum_all,string_len}` against the `parquet` control — targets: `count(*)` at 1e6 ≤ 5 ms (was 93 ms; parquet 0.7 ms; Spark 36 ms), `sum_all`/`string_len` within 1.5× of the parquet path (were 54 / 273 ms slower at 1e6 / 1e7). Re-run the analysis' §6 commands before and after on both builds (pre-fork and with the patch) and record medians, spread, floor, × floor, load.
